about: GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3 3.05bpw on one RTX 3090 inside 22 GiB of host RAM: routed experts streamed with O_DIRECT from a packed NVMe store through a ~1,400-1,650-expert pinned RAM tier and an elastic GPU expert cache, AVX2 CPU lane for cold RAM-resident decode picks, threads laid out for a 16-core / 32-thread CPU (glm-flash-lite 0bd10f3 = v4.6.1-nvme, GLM53_MODE=nvme; the entrypoint applies its small-host budget below a 24 GiB cap)
setup: NEEDS: 1x RTX 3090 24 GB (expert cache capped at 1,376 slots by GLM53_EC_MAX_SLOTS so a desktop on the same GPU cannot run the CUDA graphs out of memory); the container is capped at 22 GiB of host RAM (resources: --memory 22g --memory-swap 22g, swap off inside the cap) and runs with --ulimit memlock=-1 (the RAM tier is cudaHostRegister'ed). Below a 24 GiB cap the image's entrypoint (v4.2-nvme) applies a small-host budget: -rcs 1 (exllamav3 host recurrent-state cache 1 GiB instead of 4), GLM53_NV_MARGIN_GB=1.5, GLM53_NV_PF_RING=128 prefill read-ahead slots, and a deeper NVMe reader pool (GLM53_NV_THREADS=48 x GLM53_NV_PIECE_KB=1024), each overridable; NVMe modes are refused only under 15 GiB. The RAM tier sizes itself from the cap (1,393-1,652 experts = 12.2-14.5 GiB on the measured box, fewer when the page cache already holds part of the cap at start). An x86-64 CPU with AVX2+FMA+F16C and >= 32 logical CPUs: nv2 is pinned to a 16-core / 32-thread layout (main thread 0, controller 1, CPU lane 2-15, NVMe readers 18-31, the lane's SMT siblings on the measured box). Disk: the 125.3 GB checkpoint (only its non-expert weights are read) plus the 117.3 GB packed expert store on a local NVMe filesystem that supports O_DIRECT (xfs, ext4). This launch is NVMe-bound (measured on a 3x NVMe md RAID0 ext4 array: 2x Samsung 990 PRO + WD_BLACK SN850); a single drive or a slower array decodes proportionally slower. PREPARE (once, CPU only): the image's `pack-store` packs the routed experts (42 layers x 288 x 9.44 MB) from the read-only checkpoint into /nvx/glm53_flash_exl3_3.05bpw_experts.bin + .json, re-reads every record with O_DIRECT and checks its sha256, and byte-compares a sample against the checkpoint; `verify-store` repeats the sha256 re-read. Serving mounts /nvx read-only. MEASURED (lab.py try --on endpoint; Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16c/32t, 32 GB DDR5, PCIe 4.0 x16 with a 4K desktop on the same GPU, natural completions, v4.6-nvme): prefill 1,009 tok/s, decode C1 12.2-12.5 tok/s with GLM53_LA=0 and 12.8 tok/s with the glm-flash-lite #18 fix and the lookahead on; nvme16g on the same box with GLM53_LA=0: decode C1 9.8 tok/s. QUALITY: same kernels as the 55 GB launch: prefill / teacher-forced panel exact (top-1 1.0000, KL 0); decode not exact (AVX2 CPU lane on RAM-resident picks; paired decode KL 0.005 measured at 55 GB). Text only; OpenAI tool calls parsed from GLM's <tool_call> format. IMAGE v4.6.1-nvme (glm-flash-lite 0bd10f3): v4.6-nvme plus the fix for a decode-lookahead stall after the first max_rq_tokens requeue (glm-flash-lite #18); GLM53_MODE=nvme defaults to the N135 CPU-lane forward and the N136 decode switches (each settable to 0).
